list.heading: Workflows
list.description: Your workflow definitions, exactly as the Core reports them. Each definition is immutable and versioned: editing creates a new immutable revision, and a saved revision never changes.
list.gateNote: The Workflow contract family is published and served by the Core: the list, detail, validation, and run-history reads render here, and — by the owner's UI-30 gate resolution — the creation control is live. The editing surface waits for the Core's node-type catalogue (the Builder tab states exactly what is and is not served). No Run execution exists (the D-40 remainder); the Core serves no workflow-import member.
list.emptyAllBody: No workflow definition exists yet. The list renders only what the Core reports — no example workflow is fabricated.
list.runStatusNote: The recorded list row's run and status cells render Unavailable: the definition record carries no status member, and no run data exists while the D-40 gate withholds Run execution — never zero, never inferred.
list.failureTitle: The workflow list could not be read
list.failureBody: The Core refused or could not answer the list read. Nothing was changed; the list stays empty until a confirmed read succeeds.
list.unknownTitle: The workflow list read did not return a usable answer
list.unknownBody: The response was lost or could not be interpreted. A lost response is never proof that the list is empty or that the read failed — refresh to read again.
list.connectionHint: Check that the Core is running, then refresh.

create.nameRequired: State a name to continue. The Core records the name exactly as you give it.
create.confirmScope: Creating records one workflow definition in the Core. The Core mints the definition's identity — nothing here can choose or change it. The new definition starts with no saved revision.
create.confirmLaws: The request carries a fresh idempotency key and correlation ID (the 72-hour replay window): if the answer is lost, re-issuing the same request returns the recorded create — never a duplicate definition.
create.confirmedBody: The Core confirmed the new definition and minted its identity. It has no saved revision yet — open it to start a draft.
create.replayedBody: The keyed replay returned the recorded create: this is the same Core-minted definition, never a second one.
create.unknownTitle: The create request did not return a usable answer
create.unknownBody: The response was lost or could not be interpreted. A lost response is never proof that the definition was created or not created. The request's reference is kept below; reconcile through the authoritative list read before any retry.
create.reconcileFailed: The reconcile read did not land a usable answer either. The explained state stands; re-query when ready — the original request is never blindly retried.
create.failureBody: The Core refused or could not answer the create. Nothing was created; the stated name is kept in the form.

detail.gateNote: The creation, editing, and revision-saving controls are live per the owner's UI-30 gate resolution. No Run control exists anywhere — Run execution is withheld by the D-40 gate. The AI-proposal producer stays unwired: no proposal can be requested from this surface. The Core validates authoritatively; this surface renders Core-owned truth only.
detail.aiProposalNote: AI-proposed workflow diffs cannot be requested from this surface: the Core's proposal producer is not wired, and a request meets the Core's typed refusal. When a wired producer exists, a proposal renders as untrusted reviewable text requiring your explicit approval — it can never save, run, or grant anything by itself.
detail.stateNote: This is the family's authoritative state endpoint (a pure query). Events are never the source of truth; this read is.
detail.validationAuthoritativeNote: Core validation is authoritative. Any client-side check would be advisory and labeled as such; this surface implements no client check — the Core's typed validation output is the only truth source.
detail.validationNoDraftBody: Core validation evaluates the builder's draft. Run Validate to evaluate the current draft; the typed result renders here, labeled with exactly the object it evaluated.
detail.validateUnknownTitle: The validation did not return a usable answer
detail.validateUnknownBody: The response was lost or could not be interpreted. Validation writes nothing — the Core stores no revision for it — so nothing is pending on the Core; a fresh validation never duplicates anything.
detail.validateFailureBody: The Core refused or could not answer the validation. Nothing was changed; the draft is untouched.
detail.validationStaleNote: The draft changed after this result arrived; the result describes the earlier draft state. Validate again to evaluate the current draft.
detail.validationPassBody: The Core found no blocking errors in the evaluated draft.
detail.versionsImmutableNote: Each revision is immutable and reachable, exactly as the Core reports it. Saving a new revision preserves every prior revision; nothing here can rewrite history.
detail.versionsContentNote: The Core serves each revision's identity record (reference and creation time); no published member serves a revision's draft content, so no node/edge listing renders here — the structured graph representation renders where the Core provides the data, never invented.
detail.runsD40Note: The run history is a Core-owned linkage read: each entry renders beside the source revision the Core reports for it. The Run ↔ source-revision link is immutable and Core-owned; a missing linkage renders Unavailable — never an inferred link.
detail.runsEmptyBody: The run-history read is a Core-owned linkage read. Its producer — Run execution — is withheld by the D-40 gate, so no entry exists yet. No run record is fabricated.
detail.permissionsNote: A node's contract fields (required capability, permission, data egress, side effects, idempotency/retry safety, timeout/resource budget, checkpoint, errors, and the result where returned) render only where the Core supplies them. No per-node contract is supplied yet, so nothing renders here — nothing is invented.
detail.failureTitle: The workflow definition could not be read
detail.failureBody: The Core refused or could not answer the definition read. Nothing was changed; the page stays empty until a confirmed read succeeds.
detail.unknownTitle: The workflow definition read did not return a usable answer
detail.unknownBody: The response was lost or could not be interpreted. A lost response is never proof of any outcome — refresh to read again.
detail.connectionHint: Check that the Core is running, then refresh.
detail.notFoundTitle: No workflow definition answers to this address
detail.notFoundBody: The Core's typed refusal answers unknown and out-of-scope identities with the same response — existence is never inferred from a refusal. Go back to the workflow list and open a definition from there.

builder.helpNote: The builder edits a client-local draft. The draft is never Core state: validating and saving are explicit acts, and only a Core-confirmed save stores a revision. Every action carries a keyboard route and a pointer route, separately.
builder.threeStateNote: Three things stay distinct here: your unsaved draft (client-local), the current stored revision (read-only), and each run's own linked revision (a run always executes the revision it was linked to — never this draft).
builder.paletteSourceNote: The palette's only source is the Core-contracted node vocabulary — never a client-side list. The Core publishes no supported node-type set yet, so no type can be offered here, and nothing invents one.
builder.addDisabledReason: Adding a node requires choosing a type from the Core-contracted palette; the Core has not published a supported node-type set yet, so the add action cannot run.
builder.nodesEmpty: No nodes in this draft yet
builder.edgesEmpty: No connections in this draft yet
builder.selectHint: Keyboard: focus a row with the arrow keys, press Enter to select; the inspector follows. Pointer: click a row.
builder.connectDisabledReason: Connecting needs two draft nodes; this draft has fewer than two.
builder.connectSameNodeError: A node cannot connect to itself.
builder.connectDuplicateError: A connection between these two nodes already exists in this draft.
builder.deleteNodeNote: Deleting a node also removes its connections, so no connection is ever left dangling. Nothing stored is affected: the draft is client-local until a Core-confirmed save.
builder.deleteDisabledReason: Select a node or a connection to delete it.
builder.undoNote: Undo and redo work on this draft only (bounded history), never touch a stored revision, and the Core validates the result authoritatively.
builder.kbdSelect: Select a node or connection: arrow keys, then Enter
builder.kbdDelete: Delete the selected row: Delete key
builder.inspectorEmpty: Select a node or a connection to inspect it here.
builder.nodeTypeLabel: Node type (as declared in this draft)
builder.nodeTypeNote: The Core validates the declared type against its own catalogue; a type the active Core does not contract is the typed WORKFLOW_UNKNOWN_NODE_TYPE blocking error.
builder.contractUnavailable: Unavailable — the Core supplies no per-node contract yet. The ten contract dimensions render only where the Core provides them; nothing is invented.
builder.validationFindingsNone: None for this {{kind}} in the latest result.
builder.saveBlockedReason: The latest validation of this draft reported blocking errors. Resolve them and validate again; the save runs the Core's own re-check either way.
builder.saveConfirmedBody: The Core confirmed a new immutable revision and stated its reference. The prior revision stays unchanged and reachable; the draft's unsaved state is cleared.
builder.saveReplayedBody: The keyed replay returned the recorded save: this is the same revision, never a second one.
builder.saveNewRefLabel: New revision reference (stated by the Core)
builder.saveValidationRefusedTitle: The Core refused the save: the draft carries blocking findings
builder.saveValidationRefusedBody: The save stored nothing; the draft survives exactly as you left it. Validate to read the Core's typed findings, resolve them, then save again.
builder.saveFailureBody: The Core refused or could not answer the save. Nothing was stored; the draft survives exactly as you left it.
builder.saveUnknownTitle: The save did not return a usable answer
builder.saveUnknownBody: The response was lost or could not be interpreted. A lost response is never proof that the revision was saved or not saved. Reconcile through the authoritative state read before any retry.
builder.saveReconcile: Reconcile via the authoritative state read
builder.saveReconcileLandedTitle: The reconcile found the save confirmed
builder.saveReconcileLandedBody: The authoritative state read reports a new current revision — the save landed. The stated revision is adopted; the draft's unsaved state is cleared.
builder.saveReconcileUnchangedBody: The authoritative state read reports the same current revision the save was based on — no save is recorded. The draft is intact; you may re-issue the same keyed request (the replay returns the recorded outcome) or keep editing.
builder.saveReconcileFailed: The reconcile read did not land a usable answer either. The explained state stands; re-query when ready — the save is never blindly retried.
builder.conflictTitle: Revision conflict — both versions are preserved
builder.conflictBody: The draft's base revision is no longer the current stored revision. Nothing was overwritten and nothing was merged: the stored revision keeps its reference below, and your draft is intact. The conflict stays open until you resolve it — never resolved by a refresh or a timeout.
builder.conflictReload: Reload the stored revision (discard this draft)
builder.conflictReloadConfirm: Reloading discards your local draft and re-bases the editor on the current stored revision. The restarted draft begins empty — the Core serves no revision content to preload. The discarded draft cannot be recovered from here. Discard the draft and reload?
builder.conflictChoicesNote: Compare and merge are offered only where the Core defines them; this contract defines neither, so neither appears — nothing is approximated.
builder.conflictDismiss: Back to the builder (the conflict stays open)

guard.title: Leave with an unsaved draft?
guard.body: This workflow has draft changes that no revision stores yet. Nothing was sent to the Core by editing. You can keep editing, discard the draft, or save it as a new revision now.
guard.saveNote: Saving runs the real save flow; its outcome renders in the builder. The Core's own re-check governs what is stored.
